overview: 246-species mammals classifier, MobileNetV2 1.0/160 int8, 54.9% top-1 / 80.5% top-5 in colour, 44.9% / 73.2% in grayscale.
usage:
# Model Format

`mammals_int8.tflite`: full-integer TFLite, uint8 in and out, runs as is on TensorFlow Lite Micro and LiteRT. `mammals_int8_edgetpu.tflite`: compiled with Edge TPU compiler 16.0, every op mapped. `mammals_float32.tflite`: float in and out. `labels.txt`: one class per line, "Latin name (Common name)", line number = class index. `classes.json`: full taxonomy per class.

# Training Data

iNaturalist 2021 competition train split, 68,917 images of 246 mammals species. Initialised from timm's ImageNet mobilenetv2_100.ra_in1k. 12 epochs, random resized crops, flips, colour jitter, 20% random grayscale.

# Model Inputs

[1, 160, 160, 3] uint8 RGB, 0 to 255, no normalization (the model rescales internally). Centre-crop to a square; an 87.5% centre crop (short side to 183, crop 160) matches validation.

# Model Outputs

[1, 246] uint8 probabilities, scale 1/256 and zero point 0 (prob = value / 256). No background class.

# Model Usage

Measured on the int8 file over the iNat2021 val images for these species: 54.9% top-1 / 80.5% top-5 in colour, 44.9% / 73.2% in grayscale. Any tf.lite.Interpreter works; the GitHub README has a runnable snippet and scripts (classify.py, webcam.py, eval_tflite.py). Full hardware notes: https://github.com/mlgraham/species-classifiers#deployment-contract

# Fine-tuning

Re-train with scripts/distill.py in the GitHub repository; the recipe and what was measured not to help are documented there.

# Changelog

v1: matches GitHub release v0.1.0 (sha256 in SHA256SUMS.txt there) and Hugging Face mlgraham/species-classifier-mammals.
